stories.headline: 18 years after 26/11 terror attack, how has India secured its coastal frontier
stories.title: 18 years after 26/11 terror attack, how has India secured its coastal frontier
stories.summary: After the 2008 Mumbai attacks, India's maritime security framework underwent significant changes to address vulnerabilities. The navy assumed leadership in coordinating overall maritime security alongside the coast guard and state marine police. Integrated surveillance systems were established to track suspicious activities and improve information sharing. Recent exercises proved that while progress has been made, challenges remain in tracking smaller vessels.

article_sentences: Mumbai terror attack survivor Moshe Holtzberg is studying to become a rabbi in New York, while Nariman House is being renovated to house Chabad activities, a museum and a memorial, Rabbi Israel Kozlovsky said.

Mumbai: Moshe Holtzberg, the Israeli boy popularly known as ‘Baby Moshe’, who survived the 2008 Nariman House terror attack in which his parents were killed, is pursuing rabbinical studies in New York and aspires to become a rabbi like his father.

Rabbi Israel Kozlovsky, who is in charge of Nariman House, one of the places targeted by Pakistani Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists during the November 26, 2008 attacks, said he met Moshe two weeks ago at a rabbinical conference in New York.

“The conference was attended by 4,000 to 5,000 rabbis from across the world, and Moshe was also present,” Kozlovsky said, showing a photograph on his mobile phone of Moshe posing in traditional attire alongside other rabbis.
A rabbi is a spiritual leader, religious teacher and legal scholar.
In the photograph, the once two-year-old ‘Baby Moshe’, whose footage of sobbing inconsolably after the attack drew global attention and moved millions, appears as a 20-year-old man.
“He is currently pursuing rabbinical studies in New York and wants to become a rabbi.
Hopefully, he will return to India.
That is our hope,” Kozlovsky told PTI on Wednesday.
Moshe’s parents, Rabbi Gavriel Holtzberg and Rivka Holtzberg, were killed when terrorists stormed the Chabad House, a centre that served the Jewish community here.
Moshe’s nanny, Sandra Samuel, rescued him from the building and fled.
He later moved to Israel to stay with his grandparents.

stories.headline: IIT Guwahati develops method to assess earthquake risks in Northeast
stories.title: IIT Guwahati develops method to assess earthquake risks in Northeast
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: GUWAHATI: Researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati (IITG) have developed a method to assess the severity of ground shaking during future earthquakes in Northeast India, taking into account uncertainties in historical earthquake records and regional seismic activity.
The research was led by Prof Abhishek Kumar of the Department of Civil Engineering, along with Dr Niranjan Borah, an assistant professor at Barak Valley Engineering College.
The findings were published in the Journal of Seismology.

The team compiled earthquake records spanning 1,200 years into a catalogue of nearly 6,000 events and generated 200 synthetic catalogues to account for uncertainties in earthquake locations and magnitudes.
Using Kernel Density Estimation and Latin Hypercube Sampling, the researchers assessed earthquake occurrence rates across a geographical grid and estimated potential ground shaking.
The study found that the most intense earthquake activity occurred in the Indo-Burma Ranges, followed by western Arunachal Pradesh, central Assam, the Shillong Plateau and southern Sikkim.
The researchers also assessed eight cities - Guwahati, Agartala, Imphal, Shillong, Aizawl, Kohima, Gangtok and Itanagar.
Imphal recorded the highest estimated ground shaking, measured through Peak Ground Acceleration (PGA), among the cities studied.
Prof Kumar said the method considered local variations in earthquake occurrence and the orientation of geological faults, where seismic activity was more likely to occur.
The findings could help engineers design earthquake-resistant buildings, bridges and other structures.
The team plans to further refine the method by incorporating uncertainties related to earthquake depth and an earthquake recurrence model, a press release said.

stories.headline: Inter-ministerial central team reviews damage caused by heavy rains, floods in Jammu
stories.title: Inter-ministerial central team reviews damage caused by heavy rains, floods in Jammu
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 25: An Inter-Ministerial Central Team, led by Union Joint Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, Gaya Parsad, today reviewed the extent of damages caused by heavy rains, flash floods, cloudbursts and landslides across Jammu Division. The meeting was chaired by Joint Secretary Gaya Parsad along with Commissioner Secretary, Department of Disaster Management, Relief, Rehabilitation and Reconstruction, M. Raju and Divisional Commissioner Jammu, Vikas Kundal, at the Conference Hall of the Divisional Commissioner’s Office. The Government of India has deputed the Inter-Ministerial Central Team to undertake an on-the-spot assessment of the damages caused by the natural calamities. The team comprises officials from the Ministries of Road Transport and Highways, Power, Rural Development, Jal Shakti and Finance, and will visit the affected areas to assess the ground situation. The meeting was attended by Chief Engineer, JPDCL; Director General, School Education, Jammu; Director, Rural Development; Director, Agriculture; Director, Animal Husbandry; Chief Engineer, PWD (R&B), Jammu, and other concerned officers. Deputy Commissioners of all districts of Jammu Division participated in the meeting virtually. During the meeting, a detailed PowerPoint presentation was made, highlighting the extent of damage to public infrastructure and private property, besides the loss of human lives caused by the recent natural calamities. The Divisional Commissioner apprised the Central Team of the affected areas and the magnitude of damages to critical infrastructure, including roads, power infrastructure and water supply schemes. He also briefed the team about the restoration measures undertaken by various departments to ensure the early restoration of essential services. A detailed deliberation was held on the challenges arising from incessant rains, flash floods and landslides, which had disrupted normal life across the region. Officers from various departments shared sector-wise details of the damages and apprised the team of the measures initiated for restoration and rehabilitation. Joint Secretary Gaya Parsad emphasised the need for accurate and comprehensive damage assessment based on ground-level verification. He directed the concerned departments to prepare sector-wise damage reports, submit realistic estimates in accordance with the prescribed norms and furnish complete supporting documentation. He further stressed the importance of accounting for expenditure already incurred and ensuring that there was no duplication while preparing damage estimates and proposals. Over the next few days, the Inter-Ministerial Central Team will undertake detailed field visits to various affected areas across Jammu Division to assess the actual extent of losses and damages.

stories.title: 75 lakh fake face creams sold monthly worldwide as unregistered brands flood India via Gulf

article_sentences: Around 75 lakh Pakistani-made face creams are sold monthly in Arabic-labelled packets globally, with unregistered brands entering Kerala via Gulf baggage and seizures remaining minimal.
Thiruvananthapuram: Figures indicate that around 75 lakh Pakistani-made face creams are sold a month globally.

An executive of Poonia Brothers, manufacturers of Faiza cream, disclosed to the international environmental organisation Environmental Investigation that creams meant for India and the UAE are usually sent in packets with Arabic writing.
No agency has figures on how much of what they sell reaches Kerala.
Faiza and Goree creams do not have import registration in India.
The Faiza company also has a manufacturing unit in Dubai.
The creams reach India via the Gulf.
They reach Kerala in the baggage of passengers arriving from the Gulf.
Cosmetics are not thoroughly checked at airports.
Compared with the scale of sales, seizures in the state are merely nominal.
Under 'Operation Soundarya', launched in 2023, the Drugs Control Department inspected 275 shops.
Over three years, products worth Rs 15 lakh were seized.

stories.headline: Karnataka HC quashes FIR over alleged tampering in 2023 Sringeri election
stories.title: Karnataka HC quashes FIR over alleged tampering in 2023 Sringeri election
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Karnataka High Court has quashed criminal proceedings against former BJP MLA DN Jeevaraj and two election officials over alleged tampering with postal ballots in the 2023 Sringeri Assembly election.
The court held that the complaint, filed nearly three years after the original counting, was too delayed to sustain the prosecution.
In an order passed on November 21, Justice M Nagaprasanna set aside the FIR registered by Chikkamagaluru Town.
Police against Jeevaraj, former Deputy Commissioner KN Ramesh and Returning Officer TR Vedamurthy.
The case involved allegations of forgery, criminal conspiracy and violations of the Representation of the People Act (1951).
The complaint was filed on May 3, 2026, by Sudhir Kumar Murolli, an election agent and authorised representative of Congress candidate TD Rajegowda.
It alleged that postal ballots had been tampered with after the original counting on May 13, 2023, including ballots that had been cast in Rajegowda's favour.
The complaint also alleged that ballot box seals had been removed and ballot paper account sheets altered to secure an electoral advantage.
The complaint came hours after a recount ordered by the High Court resulted in Jeevaraj being declared the winner of the Sringeri constituency.
The original result had gone in Rajegowda's favour by a margin of 201 votes, with 279 postal ballots rejected.
Jeevaraj had challenged the election result through an election petition.
On April 6, 2026, the High Court partly allowed his petition and directed the Returning Officer to re-verify the 279 rejected postal ballots and recount all postal ballots.

stories.headline: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
stories.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
stories.summary: Seoul, Nov 26: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons, days after ignoring US President Donald Trump's offer to meet during his recent visit to Asia. Kim's statement signals again that he won't give up his evolving nuclear program — the backbone of his authoritarian rule — and is eager to bolster his country's status as a nuclear power. The North's official Korean Central News Agency said Thursday that Kim inspected two nuclear materials production factories, one newly inaugurated and the other being expanded. KCNA photos showed Kim and senior military officials walking between dense rows of what appeared to be centrifuges used to produce weapons-grade uranium and touring halls displaying what were believed to be warheads. Some of the images were blurred. KCNA said Kim visited a nuclear-powered equipment production base and a nuclear research institute as well on Wednesday. North Korea has disclosed a uranium enrichment site a few times since it showed one at its main Yongbyon nuclear complex to visiting American scholars in 2010. North Korea didn't say where the nuclear materials production factories that Kim visited this week are located. In June, when North Korea disclosed parts of a uranium enrichment site while reporting on Kim's visit there, outside experts assessed it was likely an additional uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon. Kim justifies nuke program by citing threats from US, South Korea Kim said his latest inspection visit was part of efforts to strengthen North Korea's defence capabilities in response to “variable nuclear threats approaching the Korean Peninsula moment by moment," KCNA said. He accused the US of inciting its regional allies to possess nuclear-powered submarines and committing to sharing its nuclear weapons with them, KCNA said. “The validity and substantiality of our possession of nuclear weapons and the trend of bolstering up its nuclear capability in quality and quantity are an irreversible reality,” Kim said, according to KCNA. Kim also said the deployment of low-yield battlefield nuclear weapons across multiple domains for various missions is crucial and urgent given North Korea's “inevitable reality facing the border with the most dangerous enemy state," a reference to South Korea. North Korea has in recent years focused on developing and deploying such tactical nuclear weapons amid heightened animosity with South Korea. South Korea's Defence Ministry said it takes Kim's comments on battlefield nuclear weapons seriously and added that Seoul maintains a firm military readiness against Pyongyang's nuclear threats under an alliance with the US. South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff declined to share an analysis of the North Korean nuclear facilities reported by KCNA, calling it confidential information for South Korea and the US. Kim has accelerated the expansion of his military nuclear program since his earlier high-stakes diplomacy with Trump collapsed in 2019. He has also shifted his foreign policy focus toward strengthening ties with Cold War-era allies Moscow and Beijing, seeking to strengthen his regional footing while pushing to establish North Korea as a permanent nuclear power. Trump still hopes to meet Kim Trump reiterated his eagerness to restore diplomacy with Kim as he visited China last week for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. But a Trump-Kim meeting didn't happen, with Pyongyang not publicly responding to Trump's overture. In an interview with the New York Post this week, Trump dismissed the suggestion that Kim had rebuffed his outreach, saying, “No, he didn't ignore it. You know, we had many leaders there … There'll be a time when we meet … It was just not really the right time. It was a very busy two-day period.” Trump also claimed he could revive diplomacy with Kim at any time by restarting the exchange of letters they maintained during his first term, although he acknowledged that the two leaders had not corresponded “recently.” Kim has previously said he could return to talks if the US drops its “hostile policy” against his country and respects what he calls the North's status as a nuclear state. Experts say Kim aims to win international recognition as a nuclear state so that he could demand the lifting of international sanctions. Last week, International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Grossi assessed North Korea has been expanding its original uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon, calling the move “a cause for serious concern.” Nuclear weapons can be built using either highly enriched uranium or weapons-grade plutonium, and North Korea has facilities to produce both at Yongbyon. Last year, South Korea's Unification Minister Chung Dong-young said that North Korea was operating four uranium enrichment facilities and that they were running every day.

stories.headline: 'Rural India facing acute economic distress': Congress targets Centre over rising inflation
stories.title: 'Rural India facing acute economic distress': Congress targets Centre over rising inflation
stories.summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh targets the Centre over rising inflation, alleging that higher prices, stagnant incomes and limited employment opportunities have pushed rural Indian households into acute economic distress.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh targets the Centre over rising inflation, alleging that higher prices, stagnant incomes and limited employment opportunities have pushed rural Indian households into acute economic distress.

New Delhi: Congress General Secretary Jairam Ramesh on Thursday launched a sharp attack on the Central government over rising inflation, alleging that the growing cost of essential commodities has placed an additional financial burden on people, particularly those living in rural areas.

Taking to X, Ramesh said that while the entire country was grappling with inflation, its impact was significantly more severe in rural India, where limited employment opportunities and stagnant incomes had further aggravated the situation.
"The entire nation is reeling under the burden of inflation, but its impact on rural India is far more severe -- it is in a state of acute distress.
There is a lack of sufficient employment opportunities, incomes are stagnant, and on top of that, the cost of daily necessities continues to climb due to inflation," he said.
The Congress leader argued that people in villages were finding it increasingly difficult to cope with rising prices because their incomes were already limited.
He said the decline in purchasing power was more pronounced in rural areas compared to urban centres.
"Just imagine -- how does a farmer's or an agricultural labourer's family manage to survive?

From basic food items like salt, sugar, lentils, spices, onions and mustard oil to cooking gas, children's education, medical expenses and transportation -- the cost of every single necessity is rising.
Skyrocketing prices are placing an unrelenting burden on their pockets," he said.
"Stagnant incomes coupled with year-on-year runaway inflation -- this is the 'price' the Modi government has exacted from the people!" he added.

Questioning how ordinary households could manage their finances under such circumstances, Ramesh said families were being pushed into a situation where they had to either compromise on essential needs or borrow money to meet their daily expenses.

stories.headline: Sheshnag safe: Forest Minister
stories.title: Sheshnag safe: Forest Minister
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 25: Forest, Ecology and Environment Minister Altaf Ahmad Kaloo on Wednesday said maintenance work on the Amarnath Yatra track had caused no damage to Sheshnag Lake, accusing the People's Democratic Party (PDP) of helping the Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) politicise the issue ahead of Uttar Pradesh elections. Kaloo said a 12-member team inspected the site on Tuesday on the directions of Chief Minister Omar Abdullah and found no damage to the alpine lake. “A team was sent to the spot yesterday on the directions of the Chief Minister. Later, I was apprised by the officials that Sheshnag Lake is completely safe. The Border Roads Organisation (BRO) has not done anything to the lake. The viral video is misleading, as there is a gap of 200-300 feet between the yatra track and the lake. It is a sacred religious place for our Hindu brethren, Muslims as well as Sikhs,” Kaloo said addressing a news conference at the Pahalgam Club and Convention Centre. Sharing fresh video footage of the site, the minister said, “This is Sheshnag as it stands today. Nothing has been done to Sheshnag. Not a single speck of earth has entered the lake.” He said the inspection team included officials from the Environment, Ecology and Territorial Forest divisions and the Forest Protection Force (FPF). Defending the BRO, Kaloo referred to the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed between Chief Minister Omar Abdullah-led government and BRO’s Project Beacon in 2025 for maintenance of the Amarnath Yatra track. “An unfortunate eventuality occurred in 2012 along the trek. The Supreme Court, while taking cognisance of it, ordered a 12-foot trek -six feet for pilgrims proceeding to the cave shrine and six more for those returning. The current track is in accordance with the Supreme Court ruling,” he said. Kaloo said maintenance work on the track had been undertaken after the yatra in 2022 and repairs were carried out every year before and after the yatra to fix damaged tiles, edges, and other portions. “We are checking all the parameters of the MoU to ensure they are followed. I wanted to visit the lake but couldn’t due to security reasons. I was told there was no security ahead,” he said. Accusing the PDP of helping the BJP politicise the issue, Kaloo said the two parties were “making a mountain out of a molehill” to create a political issue for the Uttar Pradesh elections. National Conference MLA and party's chief spokesman Tanvir Sadiq said Chief Minister Omar Abdullah had taken cognisance of the video circulating on social media and sought a report from the Forest Minister. The controversy erupted earlier this week after a video posted by a JCB operator on social media showed a crawler excavator being used for track maintenance near the lake, triggering concerns over construction activity in the fragile Himalayan region. On Tuesday, PDP President Mehbooba Mufti attempted to visit Sheshnag but was stopped by police at Chandanwari in Pahalgam. Police cited security concerns and did not allow her to proceed further. The video had drawn criticism from political leaders, religious figures and environmentalists, who raised concerns over the ecological impact of the work near the alpine lake. Situated at an altitude of 12,100 feet along the route to the Amarnath Cave, Sheshnag Lake is among the 14 high-risk glacial lakes identified across Jammu and Kashmir.

stories.headline: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for over 42 lakh farmers
stories.title: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for over 42 lakh farmers
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Maharashtra Cabinet on Wednesday approved free foodgrains for over 42.30 lakh farmers not covered under Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), a ₹5,548-crore provision for the Narmada-Tapi diversion project in Nandurbar, confiscation of assets of firms involved in financial fraud, and a law to regulate private-aided schools, among 14 decisions.

At the meeting chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, the Cabinet decided to give free foodgrains to farmers who are not covered under the National Food Security Act in 33 drought-affected districts of the State.
The beneficiaries belong to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category.
“The farmers will receive five kg of foodgrains per person every month, free of cost, for the next three months.
This will include three kg rice and two kg wheat,” stated a release issued from the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO).
With an aim to strengthen the irrigation system in Nandurbar district, the Cabinet gave nod to the Narmada-Tapi diversion project.
This will include six diversions weirs that aim to benefit around 26,526 hectares with irrigation while generating 11.50 MW power, as per the Water Resources Department officials.
The Maharashtra government has also approved the plan to set up a separate MPID (Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors) tribunal with a time limit of 90 days for the disposal of cases.
The Cabinet also decided to expedite the process of confiscating properties of institutions committing financial fraud and amend the MPID Act,” stated the CMO.

The State government has also decided to increase the hostel allowances for students from Economically Weaker Sections (EBC, SEBC and EWS) pursuing professional degree courses in health sciences under the Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Hostel Maintenance Allowance Scheme.
It also approved the provision of financial facilities for teachers through RBI-registered institutions.
The Cabinet approved the draft Maharashtra Private-Aided Schools (Regulation) Bill, 2026, which will be tabled in the legislature.

stories.title: Rupee falls 20 paise to 92.40 vs US dollar on crude oil spike and US tariff threat
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Mumbai: The rupee depreciated 20 paise to 92.40 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday, as higher crude oil prices and the US administration's proposed tariff hikes against India fuelled dollar demand and weighed on the local unit.
Foreign fund inflows favoured the Indian currency, but it faced pressure after crude oil prices reversed easing, hovering above the USD 95-per-barrel level, according to forex traders.
They also said the Donald Trump administration's latest proposal to escalate the trade war with major trading partners raised inflation fears.

The US on Wednesday proposed 25 per cent tariffs on imports from India, with a provision to cap them at 17 per cent if the two countries agree to a bilateral trade deal, giving it a slight edge over Asian competitors.
The proposed tariffs followed investigations by the US Trade Representative into 16 economic jurisdictions.
The USTR investigation report accused India of engaging in a range of acts, policies, and practices that create, maintain, or contribute to structural excess capacity and production.
India rejected the allegation and said the country is committed to working closely with the United States for an early conclusion of a bilateral trade agreement.
In the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 92.50 and gained up to 92.39 before falling again to 92.40 against the greenback, trading 20 paise lower from its previous close.
On Wednesday, the rupee jumped 65 paise to settle at 92.20, the highest level this fiscal year so far.
The level was compared to the closing level of 92.28 against the greenback recorded on March 16 this year.
In the past seven weeks, the Indian currency has recovered nearly 5 per cent compared to its lowest-ever closing mark of 96.88 versus the US dollar seen on October 8.
Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was at 103.79, higher by 0.17 per cent.

stories.summary: India said on Wednesday that it remained committed to concluding a bilateral trade agreement with the US at the earliest.

article_sentences: “Government of India has taken note of the Notice of Determination and Request for Comments issued by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) in the Section 301 Investigation...,” the Indian government said in a statement, adding that the notice was “currently under examination.”
“India engaged constructively throughout this investigation.
In response to the Notice of Initiation and in subsequent proceedings, the Department of Commerce stated that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector,” the statement said.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced on Wednesday that tariffs on Indian imports would be capped at 17 per cent if the two countries reached a trade agreement.
In the absence of a deal, the tariffs would increase to 25 per cent.
The Indian government reiterated its commitment to finalising the proposed agreement.

“Government of India remains committed to working closely with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement, as announced on 2nd February 2026, and in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026,” it said.
During its negotiations with the US, India has been seeking a competitive advantage over its Asian rivals.
Washington has addressed this demand in its tariff proposals.

The Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) said the Section 301 excess-capacity investigations recreated the reciprocal-tariff regime under a new name and were designed to push trading partners into signing one-sided and expensive trade agreements rather than addressing structural industrial overproduction, according to a PTI report.
GTRI said Washington's dual-rate structure threatened steep baseline tariffs against countries that refused an agreement while offering lower rates to those that signed one.

According to the organisation, the structure allowed Washington to regain bargaining power to impose duties and seek unilateral concessions, enabling a government to secure tariff relief even if the industrial capacity that prompted the investigation remained unchanged.
